corrections.form_value: Meta-analysis (synthesis); it runs no experiment of its own. It pools task performance (accuracy, error, quality) for human-AI combinations with AI defined broadly, not generative AI only, and it codes no creativity, novelty, or diversity outcome. Creation tasks (open response) appear only as a 34-effect-size subgroup of performance (PDF p. 4; Table S7, PDF p. 36). The main text does not name the creation-task studies; a search lead (unverified here) says the OSF data hold only two generative-AI creation tasks, neither scoring creativity.
corrections.source_says: Remove the final, explicitly unverified search-lead sentence from the source-based eligibility rationale. The PDF reports 34 creation-task effect sizes but does not enumerate all generative-AI creation studies or establish the claimed count of two and their absence of creativity outcomes; that count is unconfirmed and should be null if recorded. Section S2.6 describes Lai et al. (2022) post-editing summary quality, but is not an exhaustive inventory. Retain the synthesis classification and exclusion from the core dataset because this paper conducts no original people experiment.

confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion, including references and all supplementary material. The PDF is arXiv:2405.06087v2 [cs.HC], dated 29 Oct 2024, with 44 pages and supplementary information on PDF pp. 24-44; the title and authors match the form (PDF p. 1; pp. 24 and 44).

Design and context are synthesis, and eligibility.core = no is supported. This is a preregistered systematic review and meta-analysis, with no original randomized people study of generative-AI assistance and scored creativity/diversity reported (PDF p. 1, Abstract; pp. 10-12, Sections 4.1-4.2).

The corpus contains 74 papers, 106 unique experiments, and 370 unique effect sizes. Experiments are defined by different participant samples; none of these counts is a total of people randomized or analyzed, so the null people counts are appropriate (PDF p. 3, Section 2; p. 12, continuation of Section 4.1.3; p. 29, Section S1.3).

Creation n = 34 and decision n = 336 count effect sizes, not people. The creation count does not establish an experiment with fewer than 50 analyzed people; no original sample is available to apply that cutoff to here (PDF p. 32, Section S2.1; p. 33, Figure S2; p. 36, Table S7).

The publication window is January 1, 2020 to June 30, 2023, with database searches in July 2023. The databases, citation search, English-language requirement, quantitative-performance inclusion rules, and peer-reviewed restriction match the form (PDF p. 7, Limitations; pp. 10-11, Sections 4.1.1-4.1.3; p. 27, Table S1).

The synthesis pools task-performance Hedges’ g, rather than a separately reported creativity or diversity metric. Synergy compares human-AI with the better standalone performer; human augmentation compares with humans alone, using participant performance averaged across trials (PDF p. 12, Section 4.2.1; pp. 26 and 28-30, Sections S1.1, S1.3-S1.4).

S1-O2: g = 0.64, t(98) = 11.87, p = 0.000, 95% CI [0.53, 0.74]. Table S3 reports n = 370 and t(98.31) = 11.88; the form preserves this source discrepancy correctly (PDF p. 3, Section 2.1; p. 34, Table S3).

S1-O3: creation g = 0.19, t(104) = 1.35, p = 0.180, 95% CI [-0.09, 0.48]; decision g = -0.27, t(104) = -3.20, p = 0.002, 95% CI [-0.44, -0.10]; task-type F(1, 104) = 7.84, p = 0.006. Table S7 confirms the estimates and counts (PDF p. 4, Section 2.2; p. 36, Table S7).
S1-O4: creation human augmentation g = 0.52, 95% CI [0.11, 0.93], p = 0.013, n = 34; decision g = 0.65, 95% CI [0.54, 0.76], p = 0.000, n = 336 (PDF p. 36, Table S7, Type of Task rows).

The additional pooled estimates are correct: AI augmentation g = 0.30, 95% CI [-0.03, 0.62], and the measure labeled Negative Synergy g = 1.14, 95% CI [0.90, 1.38], each based on 370 effect sizes (PDF p. 34, Table S3; baseline definitions on p. 26, Section S1.1).

The relative-performance moderator estimates match: synergy g = 0.46 when humans perform better alone, with 95% CI [0.28, 0.66] in the main text and [0.28, 0.65] in Table S7; g = -0.54, 95% CI [-0.71, -0.37], when AI performs better alone (PDF p. 4, Section 2.2; p. 36, Table S7).

Separate-model estimates match Table S4: AI-better n = 249, human-better n = 121; synergy -0.53 [-0.71, -0.35] and 0.39 [0.21, 0.58]; augmentation 0.73 [0.62, 0.84] and 0.39 [0.20, 0.58], respectively (PDF p. 34, Table S4).
Figure 2 prints decision N = 344, while Table S7 and Figure S2 give 336; the form explicitly preserves this discrepancy (PDF p. 17, Figure 2; p. 33, Figure S2; p. 36, Table S7).

The AI categories are shallow, deep learning, and Wizard of Oz, supporting the broad-AI scope. The statement that more than 95% of human-AI systems involved humans making final decisions after AI input is printed in the discussion (PDF p. 31, Table S2; p. 6, Section 3).

Every numerical claim in the one-line finding matches its cited passage. The overall augmentation estimate is 0.64 in Section 2.1 and Table S3; Table S7 separately prints 0.63 in its All Effect Sizes row, an additional source inconsistency that does not invalidate the cited 0.64 (PDF pp. 3-4; p. 34, Table S3; p. 36, Table S7).
summary: The synthesis classification, version, corpus counts, and reported estimates are confirmed; no eligible original randomized people study is reported. Corrections concern company funding, missing data/code URLs, and an unsupported search lead in the eligibility rationale.
